==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{der|en|fro|discussion}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|discussiō}}, from {{der|en|la|discutiō}}. {{surf|en|discuss|-ion}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/dɪˈskʌʃ.ən/|a=RP,GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-discussion.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/dɪsˈkʊʃ.ən/|a=Northern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/dɪˈskɐʃ.ən/|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/dəˈskɐʃ.ən/|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɖɪs.kə.ʃən/|a=Indic}}
* {{hyph|en|dis|cus|sion}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{senseid|en|conversation}} [[conversation|Conversation]] or [[debate]] concerning a particular topic.
#: {{syn|en|discourse}}
#: {{ux|en|There was then a long '''discussion''' of whether to capitalize words like "east".}}
#: {{ux|en|This topic is not open to '''discussion'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|My '''discussion''' with the professor was very enlightening.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Mike Isaac and Ryan Mac|title=Meta clamps down on internal discussion of Roe v. Wade’s overturning.|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/25/business/meta-abortion-employees-discussions.html|date=24-06-2022|passage=In the May 12 memo, Meta said it had previously allowed open '''discussion''' of abortion at work but later recognized that it had led to “significant disruptions in the workplace given unique legal complexities and the number of people affected by the issue.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251101224831/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/25/business/meta-abortion-employees-discussions.html|archivedate=1 November 2025}}
# {{senseid|en|text}} Text giving further detail on a subject.
#: {{ux|en|Under each heading, you will find a '''discussion'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=14 October 2014 |author=David Malcolm|page=173|title=The Great War Re-Remembered: Allohistory and Allohistorical Fiction|work=The Great War in Post-Memory Literature and Film|editors=Martin Löschnigg; Marzena Sokolowska-Paryz |url= https://books.google.co.nz/books?id=4Y_nBQAAQBAJ |publisher={{w|de Gruyter|Walter de Gruyter GmbH & Co KG.}}|isbn= 9783110363029 |passage= The question of the plausibility of the counter-factual is seen as key in all three '''discussions''' of allohistorical fiction (as it is in Demandt's and Ferguson's examinations of allohistory) (cf. Rodiek 25–26; Ritter 15–16; Helbig 32).}}
# {{senseid|en|medicine}} {{lb|en|medicine|obsolete}} The [[dispersion]] of a [[tumour]].
